public_rationale: The categorical assertion that LLMs do no single thing well is contradicted. METR recognized strong bounded task performance, and Anthropic reported substantial success resolving software issues. These findings coexist with serious reliability problems. The assessment does not establish that LLMs had an iPhone moment; that comparison lacks a measurable threshold.
limitations: The judgment depends on reading 'well' as useful competence rather than error-free execution.
The software result is company-reported and uses tools and a restricted task subset.
Only the original dated findings are used; later additions to the live pages are excluded.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs have had no 'iPhone moment' and have no single thing they do well.

statement.excerpt: LLMs have no such moment, nor do they have any one thing they do well, let alone really well.

from_speaker: any one thing they do well
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading of 'any one thing' is categorical: no LLM performs even one useful task competently. It does not require perfect performance.
The surrounding paragraph defines the iPhone comparison as an obvious collection of useful capabilities. It supplies no objective threshold for having such a moment.

For the ongoing capability observation, use the current calendar year through publication, 2025-01-01 to 2025-06-09. LLM capabilities have no regular reporting period; this reporting window is an evaluator choice.
A demonstrated useful capability can contradict the categorical task claim without establishing that an iPhone moment occurred.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous evaluations across plausible useful applications show no task that LLMs perform competently. The separate iPhone comparison would also require an agreed observable meaning.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A credible contemporaneous evaluation demonstrates competent performance on at least one useful task or task class.

evidence.explanation: METR explicitly recognized strong performance on bounded knowledge and examination tasks while also describing failures on substantive projects. That distinction conflicts with the assertion that there is no task competence at all.

evidence.locator: SWE-bench Verified, Information about the scaffolding
evidence.explanation: Anthropic reported successful software issue resolution on 63.7% of its runnable 489-task subset. This demonstrates substantial bounded coding competence, although it is a vendor result and does not establish dependable performance on arbitrary software work.
OpenAI's evaluation supports the surrounding concern about factual unreliability. Errors in factual answers do not establish that every other task is performed poorly.
